correctness.rationale: PASS — For K_n=Ind(C_n), the standard n mod 3 homotopy types yield simple connectivity for n>=8. For a rotation r^a, a geometric fixed point exists iff gcd(n,a)>=2, because an invariant vertex orbit is an independent face exactly in that case. Armstrong gives pi1(Q_n)=C_n/<fixed rotations>, C_p precisely for prime-power n and trivial for multi-prime n. For rational homology, the generator has reduced Lefschetz number −1 (no fixed support for primitive rotation). Combined with the degree d_n sphere/wedge representation and finite cyclic rational averaging, invariants survive only for gcd(n,6)=1. For prime p>=5 the action is free; orientation on Z top class is trivial, and the multiplicative Cartan–Leray spectral sequence has an obligatory surjective d_{2m} from the top row to H^{2m}(C_p;Z); otherwise unbounded cup powers violate finite CW dimension. The surviving classes have Z[u,v]/(pu,u^m,uv,v²), |u|=2, |v|=2m−1, yielding the stated odd-degree p-torsion. Independent exact enumeration of rotation isotropy and rational Euler ranks n=8..18 agreed. The special p=5,7 cases have top degree 1 and no positive torsion, consistent with the m=1 convention; composite higher integral torsion is not computed. Finite enumeration does not establish the infinite spectral sequence argument.
